entities.summary: Albert Pighius (Pigghe) was a Dutch Roman Catholic theologian, mathematician, and astronomer born in unknown year, who lived in the 16th century. He was a key figure in the Renaissance, particularly in the field of mathematics, and his work on the Ptolemaic system of astronomy had a lasting impact on the development of astronomy in Europe. Pighius was also a prolific writer, producing numerous theological and mathematical treatises that showcased his expertise in these fields. He played a significant role in the Counter-Reformation, using his writings to promote Catholic orthodoxy and resist the influence of Protestantism. Pighius's work had a lasting impact on the development of astronomy, mathematics, and theology, and his legacy continues to be felt in these fields today. His most notable work, 'De Harmonia Musica', showcased his mastery of mathematical concepts and their application to music theory. Pighius's contributions to the field of astronomy were also recognized by his contemporaries, with his work being cited by prominent astronomers of the time. As a theologian, Pighius was deeply involved in the Counter-Reformation, using his writings to promote Catholic orthodoxy and resist the influence of Protestantism. His most notable work, 'De Doctrina Eucharistica', was a comprehensive treatise on the sacrament of the Eucharist, and it remains a significant work in the field of theology to this day. In conclusion, Albert Pighius was a polymath of the 16th century, whose contributions to mathematics, astronomy, and theology continue to be felt in these fields today.
